NoteTexAccessor::macros_defined¶

Back to Note TeX Accessor API Reference

Signature¶

TokenBatch NoteTexAccessor::macros_defined() const

Inventory Complete Local Macro Declarations¶

macros_defined() extracts the control word introduced by each complete local macro declaration. It recognizes \newcommand, \renewcommand, and \providecommand, including their starred declaration forms, plus primitive \def. Each token includes its leading backslash, such as \RR; this makes a definition inventory directly comparable with macros_used.

For the command-style declarations, both {\name} and direct \name spellings are accepted. Optional arity and default-value groups may follow the name, and their brackets are balanced before the required replacement body is read. For \def, parameter markers between the name and body are accepted. A declaration is emitted only after its complete balanced body has been found; a name alone does not count as a usable definition.

The extractor reports declarations, not their bodies, arity, scope, or final meaning after redefinition. It preserves repeated declarations and source order because either can matter to a later semantic pass. It does not expand commands, follow included files, or attempt TeX category-code interpretation. An escaped declaration command and malformed declaration contribute no token.

The result is ragged. tokens() owns a flat Text Note, and offsets() owns an Int64 boundary vector whose range for cell i is [offsets[i], offsets[i + 1]). Matrix and higher-rank receivers are traversed in row-major lane order. Undefined input yields undefined tokens and offsets [0]; any defined non-Text dtype is rejected.

Scanning is linear in source bytes and uses balanced delimiter scans rather than a document parser. Token strings are copied into result-owned storage.

Example 1: Command-Style And Primitive Declarations¶

const auto source = pluss::make_note({
    R"(\newcommand{\RR}{\mathbb{R}} \renewcommand*\vecx[1]{\mathbf{#1}})",
    R"(\providecommand{\unit}[1][kg]{#1} \def\pair#1#2{#1,#2})",
    R"(\\newcommand{\escaped}{x} \newcommand{\broken})"});
const auto result = source.tex().macros_defined();

std::cout << result.tokens() << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[4], dim=1, numel=4, encoding=utf8)
["\\RR", "\\vecx", "\\unit", "\\pair"]

The optional arity/default groups and \def parameter text do not change the reported name. The escaped declaration and declaration without a replacement body are omitted.

Example 2: Definitions Remain Attached To Their Cells¶

std::cout << "offsets=[";
const auto offsets = result.offsets().integers();
for (std::size_t i = 0; i < offsets.size(); ++i)
  std::cout << (i ? ", " : "") << offsets[i];
std::cout << "]\n";

Output¶

offsets=[0, 2, 4, 4]

The first and second cells each own two declarations. The malformed-only cell owns none.

Example 3: Undefined And Invalid Input¶

const auto absent = pluss::Note::undefined().tex().macros_defined();
std::cout << std::boolalpha << absent.tokens().defined() << " offsets=["
          << absent.offsets().integers()[0] << "]\n";
try {
  (void)pluss::note::make(std::vector<std::int64_t>{1, 2})
      .tex().macros_defined();
} catch (const pluss::Error&) {
  std::cout << "macros defined Int64: rejected\n";
}

Output¶

false offsets=[0]
macros defined Int64: rejected
